newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hino sees higher 1997 domestic sales.
newsitem.headline: Hino sees higher 1997 domestic sales.

text.p: Hino Motors Ltd said on Monday it expected its domestic vehicle sales to rise 7.9 percent in 1997 to 48,200 vehicles.
The company also said it expected its 1997 exports to rise 10.4 percent to 35,000 vehicles.
Hino, a leading Japanese manufacturer of diesel trucks, is owned 11 percent by Toyota Motor Corp.
Hino forecast its 1997 vehicle production at 50,300 units, up 7.2 percent from last year.

The company forecast that Japan's overall demand for heavy trucks would fall to 142,000 units in the business year starting in April 1997, down from an estimated 151,000 in 1996/97 and an actual 148,073 in 1995/96. The company had no estimates for total Japanese demand in calendar 1997.
